title: Inverse image commutes with internal extension along arbitrary ring objects
statement:
Let $g\colon Z\to X$ be any morphism of schemes. Let $R,S$ be commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with the sheaf tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], and let $\varphi\colon R\to S$ be a morphism of ring objects. Write $F=g^{-1}$ for inverse image of abelian sheaves [def-sfb-finite-upper-star], with its strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]; it is symmetric monoidal [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], so $F(R)$ and $F(S)$ are commutative ring objects of $\Sh(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and $F(\varphi)$ is a morphism of ring objects. Write $F_R=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ on $R$-module objects and $F_S=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$ on $S$-module objects [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. There is a natural isomorphism of functors $\Mod_R\to\Mod_{F(S)}$
\[
F_S\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\ \cong\ \operatorname{Ext}_{F(\varphi)}\circ F_R,
\qquad
F_S(S\otimes_R M)\cong F(S)\otimes_{F(R)}F_R(M),
\]
where relative tensor and extension of scalars are those of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The coefficient rings on the right are the actual inverse images $F(R),F(S)$; no identification with a ring pulled back from a point is assumed.

proof.text: Put $F=g^{-1}$, $G=g_*$. For each $R$-module $M$, [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](2) gives the balancing quotient $q_M:S\otimes M\to P_M=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M$ and its induced $S$-action. It also gives $q'_M:FS\otimes FM\to Q_M=\operatorname{Ext}_{F\varphi}(F_RM)$, with its induced $FS$-action; the inverse-image rings are commutative by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided]. By [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $F(q_M)$ coequalizes $F(a_M),F(b_M)$ universally. The index is the finite parallel-pair category, so the cited smallness hypothesis holds.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact(1), applied to the balancing coequalizer

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-balancing-diagrams] to $F$, strong monoidal by [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], and to $q_M$. Its tensorator isomorphisms identify both image balancing arrows with $a'_M,b'_M$. Thus $\widehat q_M=F(q_M)t_{S,M}$ is a coequalizer of the same pair as $q'_M$: any equalizing map can be composed with $t_{S,M}^{-1}$, factored uniquely through $F(q_M)$, then composed back. The lemma's last equation says $\widehat q_M$ is $FS$-linear for the action transported by [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. The quotient $q'_M$ is linear by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For any $R$-linear $u:M\to N$, the defining equation $\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(u)q_M=q_N(1_S\otimes u)$ and tensorator naturality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] give
\[
F(\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}u)\widehat q_M=\widehat q_N(1_{FS}\otimes F(u)).
\]
The defining equation for the other extension similarly makes $q'_M$ natural.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-equivariant-coequalizer-comparison] with $J=\operatorname{Mod}_R$, $A=FS$, $B_M=FS\otimes FM$ with first-factor multiplication, $P_M=F_S(\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}M)$, $Q_M=\operatorname{Ext}_{F\varphi}(F_RM)$, and quotient maps $\widehat q_M,q'_M$. The balancing pairs are natural by the module-map equation and tensor functoriality; their coequalizer and linearity hypotheses were checked above. Tensoring by $FS$ preserves them by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor](2). The lemma supplies the natural $FS$-linear isomorphism $Q\cong P$ characterized by $c_Mq'_M=\widehat q_M$. Invert it to obtain the requested $P\cong Q$; evaluation at $M$ is the displayed relative-tensor formula.
